Reshaping the Regional Security Equation

Political and Security Assessment

The Middle East entered a different phase of regional conflict in 2026. Confrontation is no longer confined to clear geographic boundaries or separate military fronts; it has become an interconnected web of military, security, economic and diplomatic pressures stretching from Iran and the Gulf to Israel, Yemen and Lebanon, with effects reaching energy markets and international trade.

The Strait of Hormuz sits at the center of this equation as one of the most important sea lanes in the global economic system. It is no longer just a route for oil and gas transit; it has become a strategic pressure tool that can influence energy security, shipping and insurance costs, financial markets, supply chains and the political decisions of consuming countries.

# El Nino: India gives stark warning about global food supplies in 2026

## Bookmark popover

Removed from bookmarks

* India’s foreign minister S Jaishankar has warned that the world faces an impending major food crisis driven by conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East alongside a super El Nino.
* Speaking at an Asia Society event in New York, Mr Jaishankar stated that the Global South is under severe financial, energy, food, and fertiliser strain.
* Global oil prices have surged, with Brent crude set for a monthly gain of around 14 per cent after US president Donald Trump denied easing sanctions on Iran.
* Agricultural supplies are heavily impacted by disrupted Black Sea grain exports and fertiliser shortages stemming from Middle Eastern and Russian production issues.
* Experts from the Climate Impact Lab warn that this year's record-breaking El Nino could cause nearly 500,000 heat-related deaths by February, predominantly in the Global South.
